briefs.findings: Owner-approved purpose: one reader saves articles and marks them read without losing title or address. Accounts, sharing and recommendations are excluded from version one. Design approves local Node and JSON persistence, queue-owned state and presentation through public operations. Glossary includes read articles in the queue. Sources agree and explicitly close product, stack and design decisions.
limitations: No README, instructions, standards, contribution guide, prior audit or declared next change. Main-thread research chosen because only three short files exist.

briefs.findings: Documented queue operations are save, list and mark-read; presentation cannot write storage directly. No implementation or entry point exists. Measurement over 8f70d11..81feef4 shows DESIGN.md and glossary.md added together; this does not establish coupling or a violation.
limitations: No runtime architecture to inspect or native dependency graph to analyse. No two declared plans exist for overlap comparison.

briefs.findings: No manifest, lockfile, prepared environment, tests, check scripts, formatting, lint, type or CI configuration exists. No native journey can execute. Audit inspect, inventory and measure passed using Node v24.17.0 and Git 2.54.0; these are repository discovery checks, not product evidence.
limitations: Important journey is unimplemented and unverified; no product test command was run.

briefs.findings: Approved Node stack can use the built-in node:test runner, documented stable since Node 20, with node --test. This is a candidate, not a selected repository configuration. No language style, formatter, linter or type system is established.
limitations: Only built-in runner capability researched; no runtime pin or package manager assumed.

briefs.findings: Local JSON persistence is the documented dependency boundary. No external service or integration is declared; no live service probe is relevant to the audit.
limitations: No outside integration researched or inferred.
